ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the schematic diagram, an artificial multi-layer economic forest can be seen, with tall trees arranged in rows and low ground-cover plants under the trees; sunlight shines obliquely from the upper right, the trees form shadows on the ground, the shadows cover part of the ground-cover plants, and scales such as tree height and spacing are also marked in the figure. Reasoning: The question stem states that the figure is when the local Sun is at its highest position, that is, at noon, and at this time the area of ground-cover plants shaded by tree shadows reaches its maximum at noon in the year. The shaded area by tree shadows is the largest, meaning that the noon shadow length is the longest; at the same place, the tree height is basically fixed, and the longest noon shadow length corresponds to the smallest noon solar altitude in the year. This place is in our country and is located in the Northern Hemisphere; the smallest noon solar altitude in the Northern Hemisphere occurs on the winter solstice. On the winter solstice, the Sun directly shines on the Tropic of Capricorn, and the polar circles are the boundaries of the polar day and polar night ranges; at this time, the dawn-dusk line is tangent to the polar circles.
